Itqan

إتقان — daily tasks, habits and long-term goals in one calm place
Current stage: 4 · Updated 2026-10-24
85%58 of 68 tasks

Next actions

  1. New: streak savers. Every 500 XP earns one (you can hold 2); a missed day uses one by itself and your streak on Today survives. Tap the flame on Today to see your savers, the last four weeks and how it works. Your existing history counts, so you may already hold some.
  2. Reminders and check-ins with people now reach the iPhone as notifications, even with Itqan closed there (the laptop sends them, so it needs to be awake). Open Itqan on the iPhone from the Home Screen once so it updates (data format v12); sync resumes after that.
  3. If 'Alerts from my laptop' isn't on yet on the iPhone: Settings → Notifications → turn it on and allow once. The switches above it (focus endings, reminders, check-ins) choose what the phone gets.
  4. Insights has a new Focus section and compares every number with the previous period — pick 7, 14, 30 or 90 days at the top. Tap a bar on the phone to see its value.
  5. Focus can now be for a habit: pick it on Focus, or press the timer on a habit card. Finishing checks the habit in — its minutes for a minutes habit (e.g. "10 min"), otherwise one check.
  6. Training → Routines → Program now offers "Whenever I can" (no schedule). Fixed days and Rotation still work as before.
  7. Number keys moved by one after Focus: 7 is now Training, 8 Ideas, 9 Reminders.
  8. In Settings → Profile, pick your interface language (it follows you to your other devices). All four translations have had their independent review (S2-23); if a phrase still reads oddly, note it.
  9. Record this year's achievements so far; check the suggestions Itqan offers.

Log

  • 2026-10-24S2-40, asked for by the owner: streak savers, like Duolingo's streak freeze (ADR-034). Every 500 XP earns one, at most 2 held; a missed day is covered automatically and the day streak on Today lives on (a covered day doesn't add to the count). A gap longer than the savers held ends the streak but keeps the savers. Everything is derived from the XP history by dayStreak() in lib/gamification.ts (replaces activeStreak; 17 tests: earning, the cap, gaps, today pending, backfilling returning a saver, order independence) — no schema change, nothing synced. The flame on Today now shows savers and opens a dialog (streak, best, savers with progress, last four weeks, how it works); a line on Today when savers just covered the days before, or in the evening with none left; a toast when one is earned; savers held in Insights. The active-14 badge now reads the best run, so it is never taken back. Also: useProgress now recomputes when workouts change (training XP was missed until something else changed). Five languages; checked in the browser at desktop and 375 px, light and dark, English and Arabic (RTL).
  • 2026-10-24S2-39, asked for by the owner: notifications for check-ins and reminders. On the laptop they already arrived (helper, even with the app closed); on the iPhone only while Itqan was open, because pushes carried timer ends only. Now the laptop pushes reminders and check-ins to every registered phone that wants that kind (ADR-033). PushTarget gains `kinds`, mirroring the phone's own switches (schema v12, migration tested; existing registrations get every kind until the phone narrows them). Pushes are built for the coming 7 days; a reminder or check-in may still go out up to 12 hours late (helper v3, `pushLateMs`, capped and tested); pushed text is clipped and at most 10 devices per alert, so one long note can never make the helper refuse the whole schedule. A push and the phone's own in-app alert share a tag, so they never stack.
  • 2026-10-24S2-38, asked for by the owner: Insights was rebuilt (ADR-032). The range (7/14/30/90 days) now scopes the whole screen and every headline number — XP, tasks, focus time, habit consistency — shows its change against the previous period, a trend line and its all-time total. A new Focus section: total, sessions, average session, daily average, focus days, focus streak (current and best); focus time per day with an average line; when you focus (by hour, peak marked); average by weekday (strongest marked); by area (share bar and table); what the time went to (by habit, goal or label); session-length bands; records (longest session, best day). The activity heatmap switches between XP and focus. Maths in lib/insights.ts with 20 tests (late-night sessions, hours past midnight, weekday averages, streak edges, habits created later); charts hand-drawn, no new dependency. Checked in the browser at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark, English and Arabic (RTL).
  • 2026-10-23S2-37, asked for by the owner: the 'allow notifications?' prompt appeared on every focus start — the laptop app is a file:// page, where Chrome never keeps the grant, and Focus asked each time. Now nothing asks on start; Settings → Notifications is the one place: allow once (phone/browser), a master switch and switches for focus/break endings, reminders and check-ins, per device. And a session that ends on the laptop is pushed to the iPhone: the phone turns on 'Alerts from my laptop', sync carries its registration to the laptop, the laptop signs and encrypts a Web Push for it, and the desktop helper (v2) sends it when the timer ends — no server, no new account (ADR-031, schema v11). Encryption matches the RFC example byte for byte; a real push went through Google's push service into Chrome. Not yet seen on the iPhone itself.
  • 2026-10-23S2-36, asked for by the owner: on the phone the floating + always opened a new task, even on Habits. Each screen now says what its + adds (ADR-030): a habit on Habits, a goal on Goals, a project, a reminder, a person (or a check-in on a person's page), a memory, an achievement; on Ideas it jumps to the capture line; on a project's page it adds a task already in that project. Today, Plan, Focus and Review keep the new task; Training, Insights and Settings have no +. The button shows the screen's icon with a small + so the change is visible. Phone only — desktop has no floating button. Checked on every screen at phone width.

    • 2026-10-21S2-34, a day-boundary fix: a habit's history started on the UTC day of its creation, so a habit made between midnight and 03:00 here began the day before and counted that day as missed in its streak periods, rates and the weekly review. It now starts on the local day; the same slip in a project's pace (no start date set) is fixed too. Tests build the creation time from a local just-after-midnight and just-before-midnight, so they fail on the old code on either side of UTC. No other place in the code takes a day from an ISO timestamp.
